question: Two days after delivery, a 4300-g (9-lb 8-oz) newborn has difficulty feeding and has become increasingly lethargic. His cry has become weak. He was born at term. His mother has a history of intravenous drug use. His temperature is 36.4°C (96.5°F), pulse is 170/min, respirations are 62/min, and blood pressure is 70/48 mm Hg. Examination shows midfacial hypoplasia, diaphoresis, and tremor of the lower extremities. Macroglossia is present. There are folds in the posterior auricular cartilage. The left lower extremity is larger than the right lower extremity. Abdominal examination shows an umbilical hernia. The liver is palpated 4 cm below the right costal margin. Neurological examination shows decreased tone in all extremities. Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Maternal history of intravenous drug use -> Neonatal withdrawal symptoms -> Neonatal abstinence syndrome -> 80% confidence CHAIN: Clinical features of the newborn include midfacial hypoplasia, diaphoresis, tremor, macroglossia, auricular cartilage folds, asymmetrical lower extremities, umbilical hernia, and hepatomegaly -> Suggestive of neonatal abstinence syndrome -> 85% confidence CHAIN: Neonatal abstinence syndrome can lead to feeding difficulties, lethargy, weak cry, and decreased tone in extremities -> 90% confidence CHAIN: Neonatal abstinence syndrome can cause hypoglycemia due to increased metabolic demands -> Hypoglycemia in the newborn -> 80% confidence CHAIN: Administering glucose can help correct hypoglycemia in neonates -> Appropriate intervention for hypoglycemia in this case -> 90% confidence CHAIN: Administer glucose -> Correct hypoglycemia in the newborn -> Most appropriate intervention in this scenario -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most appropriate intervention for the newborn with symptoms suggestive of neonatal abstinence syndrome, including feeding difficulties, lethargy, weak cry, and hypoglycemia, is to administer glucose to correct the hypoglycemia. This aligns with the standard approach to managing hypoglycemia in neonates with this clinical presentation.
analysis: The newborn's presentation is consistent with neonatal abstinence syndrome (NAS) due to the mother's history of intravenous drug use. The symptoms of feeding difficulties, lethargy, weak cry, hypoglycemia, and physical exam findings support this diagnosis. The most appropriate intervention for NAS-related hypoglycemia is to administer glucose to correct the low blood sugar levels.
